description: Single-panel engineering stress–strain plot, labelled only "(a)" in the top-right; no caption was supplied with the figure. Axes: abscissa "engineering strain, %" with numbered ticks at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30; ordinate "engineering stress (MPa)" with numbered ticks every 200 MPa from 0 to 1600. Five curves carry printed condition labels: CR (red), HR (black), A5 (blue), A15 (green) and A30 (magenta). CR rises almost vertically and crosses the 1600 MPa top tick within the first few percent of strain, i.e. very high strength with negligible plastic elongation; the black HR curve climbs steeply to just under the 1000 MPa level and terminates at low strain (its plateau/end point is truncated and only partially readable). A5 (blue) peaks near the 1200 MPa gridline at roughly 20% strain, A15 (green) near the 950 MPa level at about 23% strain, and A30 (magenta) near 850 MPa at the longest strain shown. An inset text box headed "Toughness, (kJ/mol) or (J/cm3)" lists A5: 1.66 (230.06), A15: 1.56 (216.32), A30: 1.72 (238.38). The figure demonstrates the classical strength–ductility trade-off among the rolled and treated conditions, with A5 giving the highest strength of the annealed set and A30 the largest elongation and highest listed toughness.

observations.observation: The figure is a single engineering stress–strain plot with ordinate 'engineering stress (MPa)' ticked 0–1600 in 200 MPa steps and abscissa 'engineering strain, %' ticked 0–30 in 5% steps.
Five curves are labelled: CR (red), HR (black), A5 (blue), A15 (green) and A30 (magenta).
The red CR curve rises nearly vertically and passes above the 1600 MPa top gridline within only a few percent engineering strain, indicating very high strength with negligible plastic elongation.
The blue A5 curve peaks at approximately the 1200 MPa gridline at roughly 20% engineering strain.
The green A15 curve reaches about 950 MPa and extends to roughly 23% engineering strain.
The magenta A30 curve is the lowest in strength (about 850 MPa) but extends furthest, to about 29% engineering strain.
The black HR curve rises steeply to just below the 1000 MPa level and terminates at low strain; its full extent is partially cut off/overlapped and cannot be read exactly.
An inset text box headed 'Toughness, (kJ/mol) or (J/cm3)' lists A5: 1.66 (230.06), A15: 1.56 (216.32) and A30: 1.72 (238.38).
No toughness value is listed for CR or HR in the inset, so their toughness is not quantified in this figure.
The figure shows a monotonic trade-off across A5, A15 and A30: peak stress decreases from about 1200 to about 850 MPa while elongation increases from roughly 20% to roughly 29%.
No test temperature, strain rate, or error bars are printed on the figure.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress–strain curves (stress in MPa vs strain in %, 0–1600 MPa and 0–30%) for five labelled conditions: CR (red, exceeds 1600 MPa at very low strain), HR (black, reaches just under 1000 MPa and ends at low strain, truncated), A5 (blue, peak near 1200 MPa at ~20%), A15 (green, ~950 MPa at ~23%), A30 (magenta, ~850 MPa near 29%). Inset text box gives toughness: A5 1.66 kJ/mol (230.06 J/cm3), A15 1.56 (216.32), A30 1.72 (238.38).
